limitations: These measurements establish behavior on one NVIDIA GB10 system. sm75 assembly verifies target compatibility, not runtime or performance coverage on every supported GPU. The 94 skipped full-suite cases remain unverified here.
The archived reference extensions contain sm121 cubins, while the Rust build uses portable sm75 PTX with driver JIT. Ratios compare these actual builds, not identical compiler targets.

Speed parity is not universal. Final dense OVO reaches 1.49x legacy wall time, continuous host OVR 1.41x, and the standard small host CSR OVO case 1.32x. The alternating CSR diagnostic is about 1.59x.

The unchanged dense host histogram path reaches 1.72x legacy for C-order float64. Owned CPU snapshot/output-copy costs also remain: default-worker CPU boundary ratios range from 0.27x to 5.42x in the short 3-repeat matrix, median 1.85x. Default Rayon is faster than Rust serial in all 8 input configurations.

Representative GPU-only residuals include float32 projected GMM up to 1.49x, sparse Geary 1.31x and one Pearson CSR case 1.33x. Full per-case measurements are retained above; passing numerical tests does not imply equal speed.

Unfiltered sparse-NaN racecheck reported 16 warnings exclusively in CuPy cupy_nonzero_kernel_incomplete_scan. A standalone CuPy-only reproducer produced the same warning class without loading the Rust backend. Native-filtered racecheck was clean.

Staging racecheck uses --racecheck-num-workers 1 to avoid a checker CPU-worker scheduling stall with pending caller fills. CUDA launches remain asynchronous; memcheck additionally checked stream-ordered allocation races.

The archived CSC extraction has racing stores for duplicate coordinates. The rare-NaN Rust extraction uses deterministic stored-order overwrite; exact legacy parity is claimed for canonical sparse inputs, not that undefined duplicate-write behavior.
